results.correct_value: The White Chuck trail is unmaintained and largely destroyed since the 2003 flood
results.evidence: The Forest Service trail page marks Trail 643 'inaccessible, no road or trail access', washed away by the 2003 flood, with no restoration planned. A 2020 trip report found the road bed and old trailhead choked with dozens of blowdowns and followed the river edge past washed-out banks. The itinerary/published-times text calling it a 'maintained trail' is wrong, and the approach presents it as a normal trail.

results.fact: saddle waypoint higher than the summit it leads to
results.evidence: The 'Sitkum-Scimitar saddle' waypoint and the approach/itinerary put the saddle at ~9,500 ft, above the Sitkum Spire summit waypoint at 9,355 ft (one topo-derived listing gives the spire 2,851 m, ~9,354 ft). A saddle cannot sit above the summit climbed from it; one of the two is wrong, but no second source was found for the saddle elevation. No patch.

results.fact: Crux pitch grade vs. stated route grade
results.correct_value: 5.5 is the hardest climbing on the route; no pitch is 5.6
results.evidence: The route database grades the Beckey Route (West Ridge) 5.5, 3 pitches, fourth to low fifth class. A detailed trip report grades it 5.5 overall: pitch 1 a short 5.5 traverse then 4th class, pitch 2 ~140 ft of 5.2, pitch 3 mostly class 4. Nothing supports 5.6; the 5.6 in pitch_detail, overview and the summit waypoint note is the outlier. Pitch 2 is set to 5.5 (not above the route grade) rather than re-assigning the crux flag.

results.correct_value: Depot Creek approach (from BC) via Ouzel Lake / Redoubt Glacier to the Col of the Wild
results.evidence: The fact itself is settled: the route database and two trip reports approach this route from Depot Creek to a ~7,200 ft camp at the head of Depot Creek and the Col of the Wild, agreeing with approach, waypoints, approach_variants and approach_logistics. But the itinerary (both days, cal, totalNote) and timing (totals and sectionBreakdown) describe the Ross Lake / Little Beaver / Perry Creek approach of a different route, with hours, miles, gain and loss all built on it; a correct fix needs a rebuilt Depot Creek day plan (and a re-check of gain_ft/loss_ft/timing totals), not a text patch, and no sourced per-day figures were established. Left for a rebuild; no patch.

results.fact: Number of rappels on the descent
results.correct_value: 3 single-rope rappels from the summit to the high notch; below it, one long double-rope rappel into the gully in typical snow-free conditions, or 6-7 improvised rappels/lowers down the gully when snow lingers
results.evidence: One trip report made three single-rope rappels from the summit to the high notch, then six or seven long rappels down a snowy gully. Another made the same three single-rope rappels and then downclimbed the gully. Both agree on three from the summit; the extra 6-7 depend on gully snow, as rappel_count_note and descent_text already say. The rappels prose presented the snow-case total as the norm.
